definition: Capabilities that are not present in smaller models but appear suddenly once a model passes a scale threshold.
details: Certain abilities — such as multi-step arithmetic, following instructions in a new format, or code generation — seem nearly absent at small scale and then jump sharply at larger scale. This phenomenon matters for scaling laws and for deciding what a model can be expected to do, though some apparent “emergence” is partly a measurement artifact tied to metric choice.
story: Imagine a factory floor where each workstation can glance at every other workstation before doing its part. Think of it this way: Capabilities that are not present in smaller models but appear suddenly once a model passes a scale threshold. And here is the clever part: Certain abilities — such as multi-step arithmetic, following instructions in a new format, or code generation — seem nearly absent at small scale and then jump sharply at larger scale. Structure decides what the model can even express — the blueprint before the bricks. And that shape of the machine — Emergent Abilities — is what makes everything else possible.

citation.title: Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models
